nodes.name: NF/CCH
aliases: NF supported cobalt carbonate hydroxide nanosheet arrays

nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis of NF/CCH
nodes.procedure: At first, all nickel foams (3 cm×3.5 cm) were treated with acetone, hydrochloric acid (2 M), and deionized water for 30 min under ultrasonic conditions, respectively, to remove surface oil and oxides. Then, Co(NO₃)₂·6H₂O (2 mmol), urea (10 mmol), and EDTA-4Na (2.5 mmol) were mixed with 36 mL deionized water under magnetic stirring until a homogeneous solution was formed. Then, the solution was poured into a 50 mL Teflon container, followed by one piece of pretreated NF was vertically placed in it. Next, the container was placed in a stainless-steel autoclave, sealed, and kept at 120°C for 10 h. After cooling to room temperature, the NF was taken out, washed with deionized water and absolute ethanol several times, and dried under vacuum at 60°C overnight. As a result, the NF supported cobalt carbonate hydroxide nanosheet arrays (NF/CCH) was obtained.

nodes.source_text: 2.2.1. Preparation of NF/CCH NF/CCH was synthesized through a hydrothermal method.

nodes.name: Impregnation synthesis of NF/CCH@CeO₂
nodes.procedure: NF/CCH@CeO₂ was prepared by an impregnation method. First, a piece of cropped NF/CCH (1 cm×1.75 cm) was placed in a 5 mL centrifuge tube containing 3 mL of Ce(NO₃)₃ solution (0.1 M). Then, the centrifuge tube was placed vertically in an oven and kept at 50°C for 6 h. After the impregnation was completed, the sample was taken out and dried in a vacuum drying oven at 60°C, and the obtained sample was denoted as NF/CCH@CeO₂.

unit_operations.name: Drying
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: dried in a vacuum drying oven at 60°C

nodes.source_text: 2.2.2. Preparation of NF/CCH@CeO₂ NF/CCH@CeO₂ was prepared by an impregnation method.

nodes.name: Nitridation of NF/Co₄N@CeO₂
nodes.procedure: NF/Co₄N@CeO₂ was prepared by a nitridation process. At first, NF/CCH@CeO₂ and urea (1 g) were placed in a tube furnace with the latter in the upstream direction. Next, under N₂ flow, the furnace was heated to 500°C with a rate of 2°C min⁻¹, and kept at 500°C for 2 h. Finally, the obtained sample was denoted as NF/Co₄N@CeO₂.

unit_operations.name: Heating
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: the furnace was heated to 500°C with a rate of 2°C min⁻¹

nodes.source_text: 2.2.3. Preparation of NF/Co₄N@CeO₂ NF/Co₄N@CeO₂ was prepared by a nitridation process.

nodes.characterization_summary: FE-SEM shows NF/Co4N@CeO2 maintains nanosheet array structure with rougher surface after nitridation; more complete morphology than NF/Co4N.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The morphology of NF/Co4N@CeO2 is shown in Fig. 1c, and its nanosheet array structure is basically maintained, while the surface becomes rougher... compared with NF/Co4N (Fig. S3), NF/Co4N@CeO2 has a more complete nanosheet morphology...

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD confirms Co4N (PDF#15-0806) phase in all nitrided samples; CeO2 (PDF#43-1002) peaks present and increase with impregnation time in NF/Co4N@CeO2 samples.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XRD patterns of the above samples after nitridation treatment at 500°C are shown in Fig. 1e. The peaks belonging to Co2(CO3)(OH)2 disappear... peaks belonging to CeO2 (PDF#43-1002) are present in the XRD patterns of NF/Co4N@CeO2(1 h), NF/Co4N@CeO2 and NF/Co4N@CeO2(12 h)...

nodes.characterization_summary: FE-TEM image shows Co4N@CeO2 nanosheet structure from nanoparticles; HRTEM reveals Co4N(111) and CeO2(111) lattice fringes with clear heterointerface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The TEM image of Co4N@CeO2 again proves that it is a nanosheet structure assembled from nanoparticles (Fig. 1f). The high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image show that Co4N@CeO2 has lattice fringes belonging to Co4N (111) and CeO2 (111) (Fig. 1g).

nodes.characterization_summary: STEM-EDX mapping confirms uniform distribution of Co, N, Ce, and O elements matching Co4N@CeO2 morphology.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 1h, Co, N, Ce and O elements are all present, and the distribution of each element matches the morphology of Co4N@CeO2 relatively well.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES shows atomic ratios Co/Ce of 1/0.140 for NF/Co4N@CeO2, 1/0.107 for NF/Co4N@CeO2(1h), and 1/0.293 for NF/Co4N@CeO2(12h); no Ce detected in NF/Co4N.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As displayed in Table S1, Ce is not detected in NF/Co4N, and the atomic ratios of Co/Ce in NF/Co4N@CeO2(1h), NF/Co4N@CeO2 and NF/Co4N@CeO2(12h) are 1/0.107, 1/0.140 and 1/0.293...

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman shows Co4N band 600-700 cm⁻¹, Co-N/Vo at ~505 cm⁻¹; NF/Co4N@CeO2 samples show CeO2 F2g mode at ~460 cm⁻¹ and Ce³⁺-Vo structure at ~600 cm⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Raman spectra of NF/Co4N NF/Co4N@CeO2(1h) NF/Co4N@CeO2 and NF/Co4N@CeO2(12h) are shown in Fig. 2a. The strong Raman band between 600 and 700 cm⁻¹...

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS confirms Co-Co (778.7 eV), Co-N (782.1 eV), Co-O (780.6 eV) in NF/Co4N@CeO2 with Co-Co peak shift to higher binding energy vs NF/Co4N; Ce 3d shows Ce⁴⁺/Ce³⁺; O 1s shows Ce-O peak.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution Co 2p3/2 XPS spectra depicted in Fig. 2b are deconvoluted into four peaks of Co-Co, Co-O, Co-N, and satellite (Sat.) peaks... Compared with NF/Co4N, the Co-Co peak of NF/Co4N@CeO2 shifts to higher binding energy...

nodes.characterization_summary: EPR shows oxygen vacancies at g=2.004; signal stronger in NF/Co4N@CeO2 than NF/Co4N due to CeO2 oxygen vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 2f, the EPR signals exhibited by NF/Co4N@CeO2 and NF/Co4N at a g value of 2.004 indicate the presence of oxygen vacancies... Importantly, after the introduction of CeO2, the EPR signal of oxygen vacancies becomes stronger...
